prompt: "In order to form my business, I used all of my savings, borrowed from the bank, and I'm personally liable for all of the debts." This is an example of which of the following forms of business ownership:
explanation: Sole proprietorship. A sole proprietorship is a form of business ownership in which the business is owned by one person. Sole proprietors finance their own businesses, run them, and are personally liable for all losses. A partnership is a form of business ownership in which the business is owned by two or more persons. A corporation is owned by stockholders, and a cooperative is owned by its members.

prompt: An important reason that face-to-face, verbal communication is an effective method of communication in business is that it provides the opportunity to
choices: have a record of the exchange.
explanation: Clarify the information exchanged. Verbal communication is a spoken exchange, and individuals who are speaking to each other can ask questions in order to ensure that they clearly understand what is being said. Written communication does not have this benefit, but it does provide a written record of the information exchanged. Verbal communication does facilitate interaction with others and a rapid exchange of ideas, but those are not always important or advisable in business.

prompt: Which of the following is a reason why you should not speak too fast on the telephone:
choices: Your caller may have difficulty understanding what you are saying.
You run the risk of offending the caller with your tone.
Your caller may become disinterested in what you are saying.
You may sound as though you have a negative attitude.
explanation: Your caller may have difficulty understanding what you are saying. Pace of speech refers to how fast or slowly you speak. If you speak too fast, your listener will have difficulty understanding you. You may also sound rude or pushy. Speaking too slowly may cause the caller to become disinterested in what you are saying. Attitude is reflected by tone of voice rather than by pace of speech. Choosing the wrong words and phrases can be offensive to callers.

prompt: Written communications in business should
choices: be clear and easy to understand.
explanation: Be clear and easy to understand. The receiver cannot always ask the writer questions; therefore, written communications should be concise and clearly stated. They should get quickly to the point by using short and simple sentences. The written copy should only contain technical language when it is appropriate and will be understood by the receiver. Most business writing tends to be impersonal, but it is not necessary to be totally impersonal.

prompt: "Greeting" guests or clients is important because it can involve not only spoken words but also
choices: providing a copy of available services.
explanation: Nonverbal behavior. Many view greeting guests face-to-face as something that is done verbally. Spoken words are frequently part of a greeting, but many other factors can be a part of the "greeting"—or the first encounter that is made with a client or guest. These may include a range of nonverbal behaviors, such as walking toward the guest, waving, or smiling. All these factors and even the physical surroundings contribute to the greeting the client receives. Singing is not generally part of the greeting process but in special situations could be considered part of the "verbal" components of a greeting. Providing a copy of available services is not part of the greeting but would come afterwards to help the guest become comfortable and acclimated in the surroundings. Making guests or clients find you should not be a part of any greeting! This creates a negative perception of customer service provided and creates a sense of frustration for the guest.

prompt: Josh and Ann operate a health care business and are considering expanding by selling franchises. Franchising their service would allow them to
choices: secure their financial future by collecting royalties.
provide various locations while maintaining a consistent image.
explanation: Provide various locations while maintaining a consistent image. A franchise is a type of service intermediary. Franchises for service businesses are increasing due to the desire to provide various locations while maintaining a consistent image and level of quality. Offering franchises would not allow them to control the prices of competitors or increase inventory or storage control. Collecting franchise fees and royalties may enhance their financial future, but it does not secure it as other variables may come into play.

prompt: If a wholesaler objects to a supplier's policies restricting trade or competition, it is illegal for the supplier to __________ with the wholesaler.
explanation: Refuse to deal. It is illegal for a supplier to refuse to deal with a channel member in an existing distribution channel solely because the channel member disagrees with a policy that may be illegal in itself (i.e., restricts trade or limits competition). Suppliers routinely communicate and do business with wholesalers, but not doing so is not illegal. Suppliers usually try to comply with a wholesaler's requests.

prompt: Which of the following is a factor that businesses consider when planning a distribution system that will provide superior customer service:
explanation: Frequency of delivery. Businesses plan distribution systems that will provide superior customer service in order to remain competitive. One factor that they consider is the frequency of delivery. Businesses want to make sure that their customers receive orders in a timely manner and when they are needed. Delivering too frequently may result in an overstock situation for customers, whereas infrequent deliveries may cause the customer to run out of needed goods. Businesses want to deliver goods at the most opportune time for customers in order to keep them from buying from competitors. The location of competitors, the arrangement of space, and the level of profitability are not factors that businesses consider when planning distribution systems that will provide superior customer service.

prompt: Why is it important for a chain of beauty salons to coordinate distribution with its promotional activities?
choices: To arrange the most economical method of transportation
To establish a relationship with one intermediary
To charge higher prices for delivery service
To guarantee a sufficient supply of advertised items
explanation: To guarantee a sufficient supply of advertised items. Chains of beauty salons coordinate distribution with their promotional activities in order to make sure that sufficient quantities of items are available when they are advertised. If a chain plans to promote a certain item or offer it at a special price, the chain must make sure that an adequate supply will be on hand to meet consumer demand. Chains may lose customers if they advertise items that are not available because they failed to make the necessary distribution plans. Chains do not coordinate distribution with promotional activities in order to charge higher prices for delivery service, arrange the most economical method of transportation, or establish a relationship with one intermediary.

prompt: Which of the following is the best example of negative horizontal conflict among members in a distribution channel:
choices: An automobile manufacturer provides its authorized dealers with rebate programs.
A restaurant franchisee uses unauthorized food suppliers that compromise brand integrity.
An engineering firm awards a construction contract to the company with the lowest bid.
A new electronics manufacturer engages in direct distribution strategies.
explanation: A restaurant franchisee uses unauthorized food suppliers that compromise brand integrity. Horizontal conflict is defined as disagreement among channel members that perform distribution activities at the same level. For example, restaurant franchisees must follow the rules that the parent company (franchisor) establishes in the franchise agreement. Using unauthorized suppliers is not only a breach of contract, but is compromising brand integrity by using products that the franchisor might consider below standard. This can create conflict among other franchisees who are following the rules. Direct distribution is the channel of distribution in which goods and services move directly from the producer to the consumer or industrial user. Since the manufacturer is a new company, it is not creating conflict by engaging in direct distribution since it has not established a dealership arrangement. A manufacturer that provides authorized dealers with rebate programs does not necessarily create conflict among its dealers. Soliciting bids and awarding contracts are common business practices and can create normal economic competition.

prompt: The number of men's suits that a dry-cleaning business can press in an hour is a measure of the business's
explanation: Productivity. Productivity is the amount of work performed in a given period, usually per hour. In a service business, productivity is often measured by the number of customers served or the number of services performed. In this situation, the dry-cleaning business measures its productivity on the number of suits that can be pressed in an hour. Service businesses often analyze their productivity to determine if there is a way to increase productivity without reducing the quality of service. The number of suits that can be pressed does not measure competence or technical skill because it doesn't indicate if the suits were pressed correctly. In most cases, one employee presses a suit; therefore, it is not a team activity.

prompt: Which of the following is a category of economic resources:
explanation: Human. Economic resources are those things that make it possible to produce and sell the goods and services needed or wanted by consumers. The three major types of economic resources are natural resources, human resources, and capital goods. Human resources are people who work to produce goods and services. Some resources are scarce, or in short supply; valuable; or international, if they are available everywhere.

prompt: The business activity that provides information needed to determine how a business is doing financially is
explanation: Accounting. The accounting activity maintains and interprets the financial records of a business. Marketing is the process of getting goods and services from the producer to the consumer. The management function determines the best use of an organization's resources in order to meet company goals. Ownership is not a business activity.

prompt: Businesses produce goods and services to sell to others by using such items as capital goods, land, and willing workers. These items used in production are examples of economic
explanation: Resources. An economic resource is any item that is used to produce goods and services. Economic capital is another economic resource. Economic markets are any arrangements for the buying and selling of goods and services. Economic credit enables businesses to obtain loans or buy goods by promising to repay the value at a later time.

prompt: A beauty salon purchases insurance to protect against the risk of burglary. This is an example of __________ the risk.
explanation: Transferring. A risk is reduced or eliminated by transferring, or shifting, the risk factor to some other person or business. When an employee is bonded, his/her employer has purchased an insurance policy to cover possible theft or loss involving that employee. Hiring security guards is an example of preventing the risk. If the business takes no precautions, then it is retaining, or keeping, the risk.

prompt: Workers in your landscape design company have decided to join a union. As a member of management, which form of union representation will you encourage?
explanation: Open shop. Open shops are preferred by management since it permits them to discourage new employees from joining the union, thus limiting the union's bargaining power. In union shops, employees are required to join unions after their probationary period. In closed shops, prospective employees must belong to unions before the company can hire them. Closed shops are illegal in all states. In agency shops, all employees are required to pay union dues but do not have to join the union.

prompt: Today's service-based economy that is dominant in many countries throughout the world accounts for a large part of those countries'
explanation: Gross domestic product. Gross domestic product (GDP) is the final market value of the total output of all goods and services produced within a country's geographic boundaries during a year's time. Today's service-based economy that dominates many countries throughout the world accounts for a large part of those countries' gross domestic product. For example, in the U.S. and Canada, services account for approximately 70% of the gross domestic product. Balance of payments is the difference between all monies coming into a country and going out of a country. Uncounted production is goods and services that are not counted in GDP because money is not paid for them. A trade deficit is an unfavorable balance of trade in which a nation's imports are greater than its exports.

prompt: Mary has been an employee at the Acme Company for nine years and has been having trouble motivating herself to complete tasks on time. Her supervisor feels she needs to develop her self-esteem through affirmations. Why should Mary write and use affirmations?
choices: To know the difference between self-esteem and affirmations
To daydream about being a superstar in life
To carry 3x5 index cards around with her for a week
To develop a positive aspect of her life
explanation: To develop a positive aspect of her life. Affirmations are positive statements about present or desired strengths. These are things which you want to accept, incorporate, or develop. Carrying around 3x5 index cards for a week would be unproductive if Mary does not write positive affirmations relating to her development of motivation on the job. To daydream about being a superstar in life does not advance Mary's self-esteem. The difference between self-esteem and affirmations is that self-esteem is the way people feel about themselves and an affirmation is a positive statement, or statements, that assist in the development or improvement of a person's self-esteem.

prompt: A characteristic of individuals who have integrity is that they
choices: adhere to a code of personal ethics.
explanation: Adhere to a code of personal ethics. People with integrity live their lives according to a code of personal ethics which gives them a sense of right and wrong. They may or may not dispute accepted facts, avoid change, or understand the feelings of others.

prompt: What is the best type of feedback to use to reinforce a behavior?
explanation: Positive. Positive feedback helps us to know what behavior is acceptable or pleasing to others. Praise and compliments usually encourage us to continue the action which received the praise. Negative or critical feedback lets us know what behavior is unacceptable or needs improvement. Internal feedback comes from within yourself.

prompt: Being alert for upcoming changes can benefit you by giving you the opportunity to
choices: try to prevent any unwanted changes.
measure the amount of risk involved.
explanation: Try to prevent any unwanted changes. In some cases, planned changes may not be entirely acceptable to the people they affect. When you are aware in advance that such changes are being planned, you may be able to prevent them from happening or at least to alter them so that they are more acceptable. Being aware of upcoming changes cannot help you to avoid those that are frightening or to measure the amount of risk involved. You should not expect to adjust quickly to change as the length of adjustment time will depend upon the circumstances.

prompt: One way that employees can provide efficient, quick service to customers is by being
explanation: Organized. Employees should always be well organized and prepared to provide customer service in a quick, convenient manner. Customers don't have a lot of time to waste. They expect employees to be knowledgeable about company goods and services, organized, and ready to work. Being organized will help employees to focus on serving customers. Employees should not be forceful or aggressive when dealing with customers. Employees who are detached give the impression of not caring about customers.

prompt: In order for the process of communication to work effectively, it must include __________ of the information transmitted.
explanation: Understanding. Understanding occurs where there is interaction and/or feedback between sender and receiver. Information is not always appreciated, e.g., bad news, nor does it always require analysis. Communication may be written, so discussion is not possible or necessary.

prompt: Service businesses often evaluate and change their policies as a result of ____________ customers.
explanation: Getting feedback from. Service businesses use the comments, suggestions, and other feedback from customers to help them decide if certain policies need to be revised or changed. Feedback also helps businesses know if their policies are meeting customers' wants and needs. Businesses would not change policies that have helped them to acquire new customers, to satisfy current customers, or to create good relations with customers.

prompt: The sales at the ABC Consulting Company have fallen recently because of a similar company that recently opened across the street. What could the ABC Company do to remain competitive and gain new customers?
explanation: Offer credit. If two consulting businesses offer similar services, one of those businesses may decide to offer credit as an added attraction in order to remain competitive and gain new customers. A business probably would not relocate or change services. Marking up prices might result in the loss of more customers.

prompt: Which of the following is a reason why accurate accounting is important to business:
explanation: To maintain financial control. Financial control of a business is the overall purpose of accounting. Accurate accounting information helps a business to maintain financial control by showing how the business is doing in terms of earning a profit and paying expenses. Businesses use accounting information to make any necessary changes in order to keep the business in good financial condition. The accounting function does not help businesses to monitor banking regulations, organize governmental support, or obtain legal information.

prompt: What type of money is recorded in the cash receipts column of a cash flow statement?
explanation: Collected. Only collected money is recorded under cash receipts. For example, if a business expects to make $5,000 from cash sales and $2,000 from credit sales, it records only the $5,000 in the cash receipts column. The $2,000 in credit sales is referred to as accounts receivable and should not be recorded until it is actually collected, otherwise the business will appear to have more money on hand than it actually does. Expenses are listed in the cash payments column rather than in the cash receipts column.

prompt: By regularly reviewing their budgets, rental businesses are able to determine if they are
explanation: Following their financial plans. By regularly reviewing their budgets, rental businesses are able to determine if they are following their financial plans. With a budget, businesses are able to see at a glance where things are off course, and then make whatever adjustments are needed to bet back on track. Businesses usually do not pay interest to customers or offer loans to employees. Budgets do not indicate if businesses receive specific discounts from vendors, although the total amount paid to vendors would be estimated in a budget.

prompt: A service business accidentally bills one customer's account for another customer's purchase. To correct the mistake, the business needs to
explanation: Transfer the charges. On occasion, a business might accidentally bill the wrong account. When this happens, the business needs to transfer those charges from one account to another in order to bill the correct account. The process often involves crediting one account and transferring the charge to the other account. It is not necessary to cancel the purchase or close the account in order to correct the mistake. Informing the customers will not correct the mistake.

prompt: What type of information would a law office post on a client's record?
explanation: Financial transactions. Posting occurs when accounting information is listed on a client's record. The purpose of posting is to record financial transactions and keep track of charges and payments. For example, a client might pay a retainer to obtain the services of a law firm. The firm posts this amount to the client's record to indicate that the client is entitled to a certain dollar amount of services. When services exceed that amount, the firm posts charges on the account. When another payment is received, it is posted on the client's record. The posting process updates the financial transactions. Law firms do not post court appearances, scheduled meetings, or personal characteristics on a client's record.

prompt: Which of the following would be done by a health care business collecting primary data for marketing decisions:
choices: Economic reports would be obtained from the government.
A customer survey would be conducted.
The company would subscribe to trade publications.
explanation: A customer survey would be conducted. Primary data are facts collected specifically for the problem or project at hand. Economic reports, trade publications, and sales records are examples of secondary data that have been collected for some other purpose.

prompt: Market researchers often place mystery shoppers in public places to observe and record consumer buying behavior. Some people find this practice unethical because
choices: observers overlook other factors that are important to the overall research.
businesses do not pay participants for their ideas and information.
most data collected from these activities are usually unreliable.
researchers are involving participants without obtaining their consent.
explanation: Researchers are involving participants without obtaining their consent. Placing researchers in public locations to observe consumer behavior is a controversial issue. Proponents of these activities claim that anyone who appears in a public place, such as a mall, is open for observation. However, there are others who believe that these activities invade people's privacy when they are not told they are being observed. Although some data derived from observation techniques are subjective or even inaccurate, it is not appropriate to conclude that most of the information is unreliable. Marketing researchers do not always pay for information; payment depends on the nature of the research and the source. For example, a business might gather volunteers for a focus group and not compensate them. Some researchers might overlook important factors while using observation techniques. However, it is not true of all researchers.

prompt: Which element of the marketing plan reveals the possible problems a service might encounter in the marketplace:
explanation: Threats and opportunities analysis. A threats and opportunities analysis is the element of the marketing plan that provides information regarding the positive (e.g., potential markets) and negative (e.g., competition) factors that can affect the business's marketing strategies. Objectives and issues are generally addressed after the threats and opportunities are presented. The action program provides details about the specific activities that are needed to meet the stated objectives. The budget allocation provides details regarding the financial requirements that are needed to carry out the action program.

prompt: What type of information is often included in a salesperson's lost-business reports that an engineering business might use to change its marketing strategy?
explanation: Why customers no longer buy. Engineering businesses usually require salespeople to complete a variety of sales reports including lost-business reports. Businesses monitor lost-business reports because they usually contain an explanation of why customers no longer buy from the business. The reports might indicate that customers are dissatisfied with the product, dissatisfied with the business's credit policies, or are getting better prices and more service from competitors. A business might use this information to make changes to its marketing strategy in an attempt to regain customers or to prevent other customers from taking their business elsewhere. The more information a business obtains from lost-business reports, the better able it is to make useful and effective marketing decisions. Lost-business reports do not include information about the design of competitors' products, reasons for local unemployment, or quality of promotional materials.

prompt: The least expensive way that a health care business can approach a marketing-research project is to start by collecting __________ data.
explanation: Internal, secondary. Internal, secondary data are data available from the health care business's own records. The business's own employees can gather these data that already belong to the business, and the business will not have to hire outside researchers. Internal, primary data are data gathered from inside the firm specifically for the research project. External, primary data are data gathered outside the firm specifically for the research project. External, secondary data are data gathered by other firms for other reasons.

prompt: A service business might conduct a survey to evaluate its
explanation: Customers' satisfaction levels. A survey is a marketing-research method that involves asking customers questions in order to learn their opinions and the reasons behind those opinions. By conducting a survey via telephone, direct mail, or e-mail, a service business can determine how its customers feel about the quality of its products. Surveys are not used to evaluate the pricing policies of competitors. Return policies are limits a business establishes for accepting merchandise for return. Service businesses sell intangible products rather than tangible items (e.g., merchandise). The break-even point refers to the level of sales at which revenues equal total costs.

prompt: Marketing strategies and tactics must always be planned and implemented with the carpet-cleaning company's __________ in mind.
explanation: Customers. To be successful, strategies and tactics must always be aimed at satisfying the purchasers of the carpet-cleaning company's products. When a company's customers are satisfied, they tend to buy more. This, in turn, will satisfy the company's executives, owners, and stockholders.

prompt: When a law firm divides all of its potential customers into specific groups, the firm is using
explanation: Market segmentation. After marketers divide their potential market into smaller groups, they often tailor their product, place, price, and promotion activities to those specific market segments. A company's competitive standing based on a comparison of its sales volume with that of other companies in the same industry is referred to as its market position. The marketing plan is a set of marketing guidelines prepared by the management of a business firm. Mass marketing is designing products and directing marketing activities in order to appeal to the whole market.

prompt: Technological advancements have made it possible for research businesses to distribute customer surveys in a quick and cost-efficient manner by using
explanation: E-mail. E-mail is the electronic transmission of messages across computer networks. Because an e-mail survey can be sent to many people simultaneously, research businesses often save time in terms of collecting marketing research. Because businesses do not need to print and pay postage for e-mail surveys, they save money. E-mail messages are one form of direct mail. Direct mail is defined as a promotional medium that comes to consumers' homes and businesses. Direct mail is a broad term that includes the mailing of promotional pieces, such as sales letters and catalogs, through traditional postal or transportation services. Therefore, not all direct-mail pieces are cost effective and/or timely. Sending text messages, including surveys, via cellular telephones can be expensive. Kiosks are freestanding, interactive devices that are generally located in public places that allow individuals to access information. This form of communication is not necessarily the most effective form to use to collect marketing information.

prompt: Identifying potential threats in the marketplace and turning them into opportunities is one reason why an insurance business conducts a(n)
explanation: Situational analysis. A situational analysis involves examining and interpreting the environmental factors that affect an insurance business. As a result of considering the environmental factors, a business often is able to identify potential threats in the marketplace such as increasing competition or a sluggish economy. Once a business identifies the specific threats, it takes steps to turn them into opportunities. For example, if the economy is beginning to slow down, a business might revise its products or offer additional credit plans to appeal to a wider market. An organizational review might identify problems within the business rather than threats in the marketplace. Training programs are internal and may be developed as a result of identifying potential threats in the marketplace. A physical inventory involves counting stock.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of how a barber shop uses sales forecasts:
explanation: To plan purchases. Many barber shops consider the sales forecast as the cornerstone of their planning. One way that barber shops use the sales forecast is to plan purchases. The projected sales figures tell the shop what amount of materials, supplies, and equipment will be needed to produce the services it expects to sell. These figures help barber shops decide whether to increase or decrease the amount of their purchases. Barber shops do not use sales forecasts to organize inventory, manage staff, or control trends.

prompt: A hair salon extends its hours to include Saturday evenings and all day Sunday. This is an example of a service business meeting its customers' needs for
explanation: Convenience. Society is now operating on a 24/7 basis. Because people work and play on different schedules, service businesses are trying to accommodate their customers by extending their operating hours, which is a convenience for customers. Service reliability is delivering consistent and dependable service each time the service is performed. Extended operating hours do not necessarily meet a customer's need for acceptance or value.

prompt: A unique characteristic of services marketing is that customers often associate the service with the
explanation: Employees who perform it. Services are actions that are performed rather than tangible objects. The employees who perform the service are often viewed as the service by customers. For example, a customer purchasing a manicure associates the manicure with the employee who performs the service. If the employee performs as expected, the customer is satisfied with the employee and the service. A customer usually is not dissatisfied specifically with the manicure but with the employee who did not perform as expected. Customers do not associate the service with the level of consumption, the object it represents, or the competitors who copy it.

prompt: Why is globalization a growing trend in the business services industry?
explanation: Opens new markets. Globalization involves doing business throughout the world. Many service businesses are expanding their operations to other countries in order to enter new markets. In some cases, service businesses have exhausted the market in their own countries and need to look to other countries for new customers in order to grow. As a result, many service businesses are entering the global market. Examples include banks, advertising agencies, travel companies, etc. Globalization does not increase inventory levels because services are intangibles. Globalization does not eliminate competitors, and often increases competition because new businesses are entering the market. Businesses entering the global market need to promote their services to new customers who may be unaware of the business and its services.

prompt: Which of the following allows a computer to search and access information on the Internet:
explanation: Browser. A browser is a type of software that allows a computer to search, find, access, and view information on the Internet. Netscape Navigator and Microsoft Internet Explorer are examples of browsers. A folder is an area on a computer's hard drive that can be set up to store specific information. A cookie is a bit of information that a web site stores on a user's hard drive. A server is a computer that provides service to another computer.

prompt: In which of the following situations would a rental business use a spreadsheet software program to calculate the effect that one change will have on its financial status:
choices: Operating profit is 15% of total sales.
Interest rate is expected to decrease by 1/2%.
explanation: Interest rate is expected to decrease by 1/2%. Spreadsheet software programs allow rental businesses to use a computer to perform accounting and other financial calculations. An advantage of using a spreadsheet program is that a business can make various changes to specific numbers and figures to find out quickly what effect they will have on its financial status. For example, a business could reduce the interest rate it is paying on loans to find out the effect that would have on operating expenses. If a business owes a substantial amount of money and the interest rate decreases, it will be able to save a significant sum in interest. The business can enter several different interest rates, and the spreadsheet program will automatically do the calculations. The alternatives are not examples of change that will affect a business's financial status.

prompt: Accepting only cash and credit cards as forms of payment is one way that small repair businesses can eliminate
explanation: Bad-check losses. Small repair businesses need to decide the forms of payment they will accept. Some businesses decide to accept only cash and credit cards because they do not want the problem of losing money because of bad checks. When accepting personal checks, there is always the risk that the check is bad and the business will not be paid. Businesses are guaranteed payment when they accept cash and credit cards. The owner of the checking account pays any applicable bank-processing fees. Debit transactions are similar to credit transactions and instantly transfer the funds from the customer's account to the business's account. Customers who do not pay their credit-card bills on time are responsible for late-payment costs.

prompt: The customers have gone, and Chris and Alex are closing their leasing business for the night at 9:00 p.m. Good safety and security measures for them to follow would be to
choices: approach anyone in the vicinity who looks suspicious.
lock all doors before completing housekeeping chores.
have one person stay late to check doors and windows.
empty trash into the dumpster and clean outside areas.
explanation: Lock all doors before completing housekeeping chores. Once customers have gone, the owners should lock all doors before doing other chores such as straightening up the office or doing paperwork. Keeping the doors locked will prevent unwanted or potentially dangerous people from entering the building. One person should not stay late or do outside chores after closing time. This makes them less vulnerable to robbery or attack. If anyone in the area seems suspicious, the owners should drive away and then telephone the police from another location.

prompt: What should all companies have on the premises in order to handle accidents?
explanation: First-aid supplies. Companies of all sizes should have adequate first-aid supplies available for use in the event that accidents occur. Basic first-aid supplies enable employees to provide immediate treatment to an injured or ill person until medical help is available. Employees should know where the supplies are located in order to administer basic first aid as quickly as possible. Most businesses do not have emergency personnel, hospital equipment, or trained technicians on the premises, although some large corporations maintain an in-house medical facility.

prompt: Preventing security problems is important to services businesses because the financial losses from these problems may force the businesses to
explanation: Close. Security problems are a risk to services businesses because the financial losses they cause are sometimes so large that the businesses are forced to close. Therefore, businesses try to prevent security problems in order to succeed. A business faced with financial losses because of security problems would not be able to expand. Reorganizing and moving would not prevent financial losses unless the security problems were solved.

prompt: The process of converting resources into goods and services is called
explanation: Production. This process makes resources more useful to ultimate consumers and industrial users. Marketing is all those functions involved in getting goods, services, and ideas to the final user. Refinement is the process of making ongoing product improvements. Entrepreneurship involves taking the risks of business ownership.

prompt: A daily list of activities to be completed is referred to as a __________ list.
explanation: To-do. Each day, you should review your weekly master list and then list on a separate sheet of paper work to do the following day. By writing down everything you want to accomplish during a specific time period, you have created a list of goals. A master list is a complete listing of all the activities that need to be accomplished.

prompt: A law firm employee purchases $1,750 worth of office supplies and receives an invoice offering a 2% discount for paying within 15 days. If the employee pays the invoice within that time, the firm will save
explanation: $35. Employees who have responsibility for buying office supplies and paying invoices are in a good position to help the law firm control expenses. If an employee receives an invoice offering a discount for paying within a certain period of time and takes advantage of the discount, the business will save money. In this situation, the law firm will save $35 because 2% of $1,750 is $35. Calculate the savings by multiplying the amount of the invoice by the percentage of discount ($1,750 x 2% or .02 = $35).

prompt: Individuals can improve their chances of making a good first impression on others by
choices: wearing dressy clothes at all times.
explanation: Sitting up straight. Individuals are frequently judged by others on the basis of first impressions or the image they project. Good posture has a positive effect on the image people project to others, and sitting up straight is an example of good posture. Using slang will not create a favorable impression. Wearing dressy clothes at all times is inappropriate and may indicate poor judgment. Not letting the other person talk makes a bad impression.

prompt: Which of the following is an important benefit of setting goals:
choices: Increases your chances of success in life
explanation: Increases your chances of success in life. Success has been defined as reaching the goals you have set yourself. Setting goals helps you to achieve success by helping you to understand yourself, giving you a target to aim toward, raising your level of self-esteem, and giving you a way to measure your progress. Goals should be accepted as your own, not set to please others. Goals provide valuable guidelines, not restrictions. Not all goals make life simpler.

prompt: During a workplace negotiation, each person agrees to give up something to reach an agreement. This is often called a
explanation: Compromise. Negotiation is the process of reaching an agreement with another party. In any negotiation, one person attempts to get another person to agree to a certain course of action to meet one person's needs or wants. Compromise occurs when an agreement is reached by giving up something in order to obtain something else. Deadlock occurs when two people cannot reach an agreement. A dispute is a disagreement. A guarantee is a promise that a business makes to a consumer stating that a product's purchase price will be refunded if the product is not satisfactory.

prompt: What type of requirements for business careers varies greatly depending on the specific job?
explanation: Educational. There are many different jobs in business, and each job has specific educational requirements. For example, employees who are involved in accounting and bookkeeping need different training than those involved in advertising or visual merchandising. Furthermore, different jobs within the same career category often require different training. For example, an advertising employee who writes ad copy needs different training than the employee who illustrates the ad. Employees usually decide which personal, financial, and social aspects of the job are important to them.

prompt: Which of the following is a guideline to follow in writing a follow-up letter after a job interview:
choices: Make the letter chatty and personal.
Review your job skills in detail.
explanation: Be brief, concise, and prompt. A follow-up letter after a job interview should be businesslike, not chatty and personal. It should be written on plain stationery of a subdued color, not on colorful notepaper. It should also be very short, to the point, sent promptly after the interview, and appreciative of the time the interviewer gave you.

prompt: What is the preferred length of a job resume?
explanation: From one to two pages. The preferred length of a resume is one page-or two pages if absolutely necessary. The most effective resumes stress the high points of the applicant's qualifications in a brief format. People who are responsible for reading the resumes do not want to spend a great amount of time trying to find out if the applicant is qualified for the position. Therefore, resumes should never be three or five pages in length. Applicants should be able to condense their experiences into a brief format and not write resumes that are as long as necessary.

prompt: Which of the following is often the most important factor that insurance businesses consider when deciding which employee to promote:
choices: Length of time with the company
explanation: Rating on performance appraisal. When an insurance business promotes from within, it often reviews the performance appraisal of each employee who is in line for the position. The employee who has consistently received an excellent appraisal usually is offered the promotion because that employee has demonstrated ability. Businesses generally believe that employees who receive positive appraisals are capable of assuming more responsibility and deserve to be promoted. Some businesses may consider an employee's time on the job, but the deciding factor usually is performance. Businesses do not consider fringe benefits when making decisions about promotions. Businesses consider personal references during the initial hiring process but not for promotions.

prompt: The benefit of registering on a professional organization's web site is to
choices: speed up the time it takes to download materials.
gain information not available to the general public.
find out about the organization's privacy policies.
access the organization's home page after hours.
explanation: Gain information not available to the general public. Many professional organizations require visitors to register on their web sites before accessing valuable information about job opportunities, skill development, and marketing trends. Because the registration provides demographic data such as the names and e-mail addresses of people visiting the site, it can be an important tool for marketing to new members. Faster computer equipment (e.g., modem and processor) will speed up download time, not web-site registration. Home pages are the entry points into a professional organization's web site, and they are accessible to everyone regardless of their registration status. Likewise, privacy policies are available to all visitors because they give an explanation of how the organization plans to collect and use data.

prompt: Which of the following is a cost that a chain of beauty salons builds into the price of its goods:
explanation: Distribution. There are a variety of distribution paths, or routes, that a chain of beauty salons can use to move its goods or services to their final destination. Chains use trucks, planes, trains, and ships to move products. The cost of each type of transportation varies. Chains choose the method that fits within their price range because the distribution costs are built into the price of the product. Receivables are all monies owed to a chain by its customers. Consignment is a purchase arrangement whereby products are sent to a retailer who pays for the products only upon their sale. Orientation is job preparation or induction training for new employees.

prompt: A health spa might be involved in the illegal activity of deceptive pricing if it
choices: misleads customers about the true value of a service.
sells health products at a limited number of predetermined price points.
changes prices according to current demand.
offers special prices on a discontinued health item.
explanation: Misleads customers about the true value of a service. Deceptive pricing is an illegal pricing tactic because it misleads customers about the true value of a good or service. An example of deceptive pricing is setting a high price on a health service and then advertising a big discount which actually reduces the price to a realistic, or normal, level. Customers buy the service because they think they are saving money when, in fact, they are paying what the service is actually worth. Price lining involves selling products at a limited number of predetermined price points. Variable pricing involves changing prices according to current demand. Promotional pricing involves offering special prices on certain products such as discontinued items. These pricing activities are not illegal.

prompt: Which of the following is considered legal in all states:
choices: Selling products below cost in order to attract customers to the business
Agreeing on a product's price with other businesses that sell the product
Showing the price per unit along with the total price of the item
Treating channel members differently as to the terms and conditions of sale
explanation: Showing the price per unit along with the total price of the item. Unit pricing is considered legal in all states. In some states, government regulations require businesses to use this form of pricing because it makes it much easier for consumers to compare the value of products. However, this is an added expense for businesses because of the time required to calculate unit prices, print labels, and post prices. Businesses are not allowed to use price discrimination, which involves charging different prices to similar customers who are buying the same products, if doing so would damage competition. Therefore, all channel members must be treated equally as to the terms and conditions of sale. Agreeing on a product's price with other businesses that sell the product is price fixing and is not allowed by the government. Many states have minimum price laws intended to keep retailers from selling products below cost.

prompt: A factor that businesses consider when pricing services is the target customer's __________ the service.
explanation: Perceived value of. Businesses usually consider customers' perception of value when pricing services. If customers believe that certain services are valuable, they usually are willing to pay more for them than services they think have less value. For example, medical treatment is often expensive but consumers are willing to pay the price when they are sick or injured. On the other hand, a consumer might not see the value of staying in a high-priced, luxury hotel when an economical motel is available. The economy motel would not set a high price on its rooms because its target customers would not perceive a value. Businesses do not consider a customer's ability to pay for, involvement in, or understanding of the service when setting prices.

prompt: Directing and guiding all stages in the life cycle of a product is part of
explanation: Product/Service management. Product/Service management involves obtaining, developing, maintaining, and improving a product or service mix in response to market opportunities. It involves decision making—from the development of a product until it is removed from the market. Concept testing is the process of exploring the concept, or idea, for a product in order to obtain feedback. Product development is the stage in the creation of a new product in which a working model may be tested, modified, and retested. Marketing-information management is the marketing function that involves gathering, accessing, synthesizing, evaluating and disseminating information for use in making business decisions.

prompt: A characteristic of the growth stage of a product's life cycle is
explanation: Rising sales. A product in the growth stage of the product life cycle has been accepted by consumers, and sales are increasing. Product production is more efficient at this stage, resulting in lower costs of production. Distribution expands as the market expands. Obsolescence does not begin until the product is in late maturity or decline.

prompt: What is one way that services businesses are using the information that they are able to obtain due to the advances in Internet technology?
explanation: To compile customer databases. Services businesses often use Internet technology to obtain valuable information about customers. Today, many businesses maintain web sites that are visited by many users who may be potential customers. When users visit the sites, the businesses often ask them to register in order to access the site. Then, the registration process involves answering a series of questions such as name, street address, e-mail address, personal interests, business associations, etc. The businesses compile this information into customer databases that they can use to send additional information to those visitors who fit the criteria of their target markets. Businesses do not use the information that they are able to obtain due to the advances in Internet technology to develop production systems, interview potential employees, or prepare operating policies.

prompt: Ethical repair shops establish procedures to handle consumer complaints and returns.
choices: False, establishing procedures is not important unless required by law.
True, establishing procedures reduces harmful effects to the shop and its image.
False, establishing procedures is a waste of time if products have been tested for safe use.
True, establishing procedures is a way of explaining problems with products because of improper use by customers.
explanation: True, establishing procedures reduces harmful effects to the shop and its image. Not only is it ethical to have procedures for handling complaints and returns, it is also in the best interest of the repair shop. However, these procedures are not required by law. Ethical repair shops want to resolve any problems and provide safe products to customers. Ethical repair shops do not blame customers for problems or believe that procedures are a waste of time or not important.

prompt: Trends in new-service development are influenced greatly by advances in
explanation: Technology. Advances in technology continue to open the door to the development of more new and innovative services. Services that were unknown only a few years ago are commonplace today. An example is text-messaging and the ability to send photos by way of cellular phones. As technology continues to advance, the possibilities for more new services also grows. Businesses are using this technology to develop unique services that will attract customers. Advances in manufacturing and in production allow businesses to develop new tangible goods rather than services. Many customers must be educated about the benefits of technologically advanced services.

prompt: Which of the following safeguards consumers by preventing rental businesses from using false and deceptive advertisements:
explanation: Federal Trade Commission Act. This act was passed in 1914 and established the Federal Trade Commission, which administers laws that forbid false, misleading, or deceptive advertising of consumer products. The Sherman Antitrust Act is intended to prevent monopolies and price fixing. The Robinson-Patman Act forbids businesses from discriminating in the prices or services offered to competing customers. The Clayton Act is intended to prevent specific business actions that might prohibit competition.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a combination of a good and a service offered at a beauty salon:
choices: On-time appointment and a free consultation
Magazines in the waiting area and a clean salon
Manicure and a bottle of nail polish for at-home use
explanation: Manicure and a bottle of nail polish for at-home use. Both goods and services are products. Goods refer to tangible objects that can be manufactured or produced for resale, and services are intangible objects that can be sold. The only tangible object in the list of answer choices is the bottle of nail polish. After purchase, the polish can be taken home for personal consumption. The second part of the combination, the manicure, is an intangible service that is performed by a nail technician. A shampoo and a haircut are intangible services that are typically performed by a hair stylist. This is also true of the on-time appointment and the free consultation. Magazines in the waiting area and a clean salon are activities or benefits (i.e., customer service) offered at beauty salons in order to create goodwill.

prompt: Which of the following is a reason that a business would make changes to its services:
choices: To spread risk over a wider area
To keep up with changing consumer preferences
To predict the success of the changed service
To make room for other goods and services
explanation: To keep up with changing consumer preferences. Consumers' attitudes toward services change over time, and their preference for a service may change. Altering the service in some way can renew customers' interest. Making room for other goods and services is a reason for using the contraction strategy. By adding services to the product mix, businesses are able to spread risk over a wider area. A limitation to the alteration strategy is that businesses cannot predict the success of altered services.

prompt: Brand or trade names are used primarily to identify a
explanation: Product. The primary reasons that brands are used are for identification and differentiation. Brand names identify products and separate them from similar products. Standards are specifications or statements that are used as a basis for comparing or judging goods or services. A market is a customer or a potential customer who has an unfulfilled desire and is financially able and willing to satisfy that desire. A trend is the general direction in which people or events are moving.

prompt: How can a service business best handle customers' complaints and problems?
choices: Obtain help from outside sources to resolve customer service problems and issues.
Require that all employees handle all customer complaints and problems the same way.
Train employees and provide them with some flexibility and authority to make decisions.
Provide customers the opportunity to discuss their problems with upper management.
explanation: Train employees and provide them with some flexibility and authority to make decisions. When customers have complaints or problems with a business's services, it is important to take steps to fix the problem. The key to service recovery is to train employees to handle a variety of customers and situations, to advise them about the company's guidelines and policies, and to give them some authority to make decisions in certain routine situations. Since service problems vary by situation, customers behave in different ways, and managers are not always available to approve a minor action, it is in the best interest of the company to let the frontline employee use his/her judgment to resolve routine problems quickly in order to satisfy the customer. Because outsourcing can be expensive and because customers want to resolve their problems quickly, complaints are usually handled by the service business. Routine problems and complaints do not usually require upper management involvement.

prompt: When purchasing services, price is an important consideration when a customer feels that s/he has many similar
explanation: Options. Because services do not have physical characteristics or attributes, the price of a service is one of the few signals available for customers when making a purchasing decision. In many cases, customers perceive the more expensive services as possessing higher quality. When several companies offer similar services at comparable prices, the price becomes a strong factor because customers have more options from which to choose. The customer often sees the comparable pricing among services as an indication of comparable or similar quality. Therefore, the customer feels that s/he is not sacrificing quality for price when selecting a lower-priced service. Competitors are rival businesses that seek to attract the same scarce customer dollars. Customers base their opinions about a service on several factors including price, quality, and satisfaction. The amount of perceived risk is personal and varies by situation. Therefore, it cannot be assumed that most customers will choose price over quality when some degree of risk is usually involved with both service price and service quality.

prompt: Advertising agencies are independent service businesses that
explanation: Prepare advertising for clients. An advertising agency is an independent service business that specializes in preparing advertising and other types of promotion and providing related services. Its clients may be individuals, organizations, or businesses. Agencies charge commissions, markups, or fees for all of their services. They may operate within a specific geographic area, or they may have clients in all parts of the world. Agencies do not train advertisers.

prompt: Some insurance companies promote good health by suggesting changes in dietary and exercise habits. This is an example of __________ promotion.
explanation: Public-service. This is a type of institutional promotion that informs consumers about noncontroversial issues that are in the public's interest. Insurance companies have a vested interest in public health. Public-relations promotions deal with controversial public issues that are related to a company or its products. Primary product promotion is intended to stimulate demand for an entire class of goods and services. Patronage promotion is a type of institutional promotion designed to promote a firm's features or prestige.

prompt: The communication methods chosen by an engineering business are referred to as the business's
explanation: Promotional mix. The promotional mix is a combination, or blend, of marketing communication channels that an engineering business uses to send its messages to consumers. Advertising is any paid form of nonpersonal presentation of ideas, goods, or services. Visual merchandising is display. Advertising and visual merchandising may be parts of the promotional mix. The marketing mix is a combination of product, price, place, and promotion used to attract customers to a business.

prompt: To be ethical, sweepstakes should clearly state
choices: how widely the sweepstakes offer has been distributed.
explanation: That no purchase is necessary. This is a requirement in order to be classified as a sweepstake. A sweepstake is a game of chance, and everyone who enters has an opportunity to win. Ethical sweepstakes do not require consumers to make purchases. Although information about prizes and odds of winning might be included as a matter of enticement, the ethical question deals with the purchase.

prompt: When governments develop and enforce laws relating to deceptive advertisements, they are regulating a health care business's __________ activities.
explanation: Promotional. Promotion is the marketing element that involves the various types of communications that marketers use to inform, persuade, or remind customers of their products. Advertising is a nonpersonal, paid form of promotion. To protect consumers from misleading or deceptive advertising, governments develop and enforce laws that regulate how businesses can promote their products. Distribution refers to the activities that involve moving or transferring ownership of products from producers to consumers. Financial activities involve the allocation of funds to operate a business. Research activities involve collecting and analyzing data.

prompt: Which of the following limits the usefulness of the Internet as an advertising tool:
explanation: E-mail filter. An e-mail filter prevents messages with unfamiliar addresses from reaching an inbox. This means that an unsolicited advertisement is likely to never reach the intended recipient. Personalization has a positive impact on advertising because businesses can send e-mails with a recipient's name in the body of the message or direct targeted ads based on visitor behavior. Action and sound capabilities make Internet ads more memorable, much like television commercials. Linking allows a user to access an advertiser's web site, thereby increasing the likelihood of a purchase decision.

prompt: Which of the following parts of a print ad often creates an image that people come to associate with that insurance business:
explanation: Logotype. The logotype is the name and/or symbol used by an insurance business. Businesses believe that having a unique logotype creates an image that people will come to recognize and associate with that business. The logotype clearly identifies the product's brand or advertiser to consumers. An illustration is a photograph, drawing, painting, or graphic such as a chart, table, or graph. A headline is text set in large type and usually positioned at the top of an advertisement. A photograph is an illustration.

prompt: A personalized fax message that is sent to a rental business is an example of a promotional strategy called
explanation: Direct mail. Direct mail is defined as promotional messages that are sent directly to consumers' homes and businesses. Direct mail appears in many forms, including messages that come to businesses via the fax machine. Electronic commerce is the buying and selling of goods and services over the Internet. Telecom marketing and indirect solicitation are not terms that are commonly used to describe a promotional strategy.

prompt: Which of the following might a business lose if it fails to inform its employees about the goods and services being promoted:
explanation: Sales. The purpose of coordinating promotional activities is to bring customers into the business and increase sales. Informing employees about the goods and services being promoted is an activity that should be coordinated. If employees are not aware of the promotion or the goods and services being promoted, they will not be able to help customers and persuade them to buy. By not informing employees about the goods and services being promoted, the business runs the risk of losing sales. Image is the way in which a business is viewed by others. Basics are staple goods. Credit is the ability to obtain products or money based on a promise to pay later.

prompt: A service business effectively uses integrated communications by coordinating all of the elements that make up the __________ mix.
explanation: Marketing. The marketing mix is the combination of the four elements of marketing—product, place, promotion, and price. Integrated marketing communications refers to the coordination of clear and unified messages that a business distributes through various message channels to its customers and to the public about itself and its products. Successful integrated marketing communications make sure that each message channel (e.g., brochures, web site, broadcast advertisement) conveys the same information to provide clear, unified (consistent) messages. Management is a business activity. Sales are part of the marketing function. Product mix is the particular assortment of goods and services that a business offers in order to meet its market's needs and its company's goals.

prompt: Selling helps customers to determine their needs by providing an opportunity for
explanation: Two-way communication. Salespeople use two-way communication to determine customer needs so that they can suggest appropriate products. This communication process helps to clarify in customers' minds exactly what their needs are. The overall role of selling includes adding utility, increasing employment, and promoting competition.

prompt: What is a benefit to insurance businesses of using selling policies?
choices: Selling policies can be used to assess sales staff performance.
The use of selling policies reduces customer objections.
The use of selling policies usually decreases job satisfaction.
explanation: Selling policies can be used to assess sales staff performance. Other benefits of using selling policies include preventing misunderstandings, reducing confusion for employees, keeping salespeople from having to make decisions on their own, making sure appropriate action is taken when necessary, assuring that customers receive fair and equal treatment, enhancing employee loyalty, increasing job satisfaction, and contributing to a more pleasant work experience. Customer objections may not be reduced by selling policies.

prompt: What cost-effective tool is often used by salespeople who sell time-share plans and provides product information to customers that they can view on personal computers?
explanation: Multimedia disks. The disks can be inserted in a computer so the customer can view product information such as catalogs, diagrams, specifications, and testimonials. Audio disks are not visual in nature. Transparencies are generally viewed with overhead projectors. Micro bite is not a legitimate term to describe a tool to view information on a personal computer.

prompt: One way that governments often control selling practices in a private enterprise system is by
choices: mandating that all businesses structure ownership as corporations.
establishing regulations that make it difficult to enter a specific market.
reviewing each sales transaction that exceeds a set amount in dollars and volume.
requiring that all businesses provide government access to their computer databases.
explanation: Establishing regulations that make it difficult to enter a specific market. A private enterprise system is an economic system in which individuals and groups, rather than government, own or control the means of production—the human and natural resources and capital goods used to produce goods and services. Many governments develop regulations and act as referee between producers, intermediaries, and consumers. Establishing regulations can make it difficult to enter a given market, but not impossible. Mandating ownership structure and requiring government access to business information are not characteristics of a private or semiprivate enterprise system. It is unrealistic to expect a government in a large private enterprise system to review each sales transaction that occurs.

prompt: What type of product information might a salesperson who sells dry-cleaning equipment be able to obtain from a manufacturer's representative?
explanation: How the product is made. Manufacturers' representatives can provide salespeople who sell dry-cleaning equipment with detailed information about the manufacturing process. They can explain why certain materials and procedures are used. Salespeople who understand how products are made are better able to pass on this information to customers and encourage them to buy. The salesperson's company would decide what type of credit terms to make available and what inventory method to use. A manufacturer's representative might not know how a product became popular.

prompt: One reason why customers often perceive a higher level of risk when buying services than when buying goods is because the service experience is
explanation: Different for each customer. Although the service may be the same, they way each customer experiences the service may be different. Depending on the customer and his/her perceptions, the service may be of high quality or of lower quality. For example, one customer joins a health club and is satisfied with the facilities and the programs that are offered while another customer is less than satisfied. The services are the same, but the experiences are different. Therefore, there is more risk involved in buying services because all customers will not experience them in the same way. Services are not standardized by industry, although the services within an industry may be very similar. Services are not difficult to understand. Providers often guarantee that customers will be satisfied with the services they receive and may offer to refund their money if they are not.

prompt: What do home-security salespeople need to explain to customers to persuade them to buy services?
explanation: Benefits. Customers do not buy features; they buy benefits. In order to persuade customers to buy, home-security salespeople need to be able to translate the features of their services in terms of benefits to the individual customer. By explaining the benefits of those services, salespeople will enable customers to understand the differences between their services and those of their competitors. A feature is a fact or characteristic of the product. Warranties and uses are product features.

prompt: Diane sells costume jewelry in a department store and her friend Linda sells life insurance. Given these facts, which of the following statements is true about the selling process each uses:
choices: Linda often skips one or more phases of the selling process.
The selling process is identical for both types of sales.
Linda spends more time than Diane on closure.
Diane does not need to prescribe solutions to customer needs.
explanation: Linda spends more time than Diane on closure. This is because customers may raise more objections or have more questions when considering the purchase of an expensive, intangible product such as life insurance. Linda also spends more time than Diane on each phase of the selling process because of the nature of her product, and she is not likely to skip any of the phases. Diane may spend less time on the entire sales process but often must respond to customers' questions about the features of the jewelry.

prompt: A sales greeting used to create a friendly atmosphere is known as the __________ approach.
explanation: Welcome. The welcome approach is intended to make customers feel at home in the business. An example of a welcome approach is, "Good morning, Ms. Jackson." A service approach is a polite question that indicates willingness to be of service to the customer. The merchandise approach is a comment or question about the merchandise at which a customer is looking. The combination approach is an opening statement which combines two or more of the other approaches.

prompt: Which of the following is a factor that influences both consumer and organizational buying behavior:
explanation: Economics. Economics is a factor that influences both consumer and organizational buying behavior because both need sufficient income to make purchases. Consumers' level of income affects what they buy and the price of those items. Consumers with more income are able to buy expensive luxury items while those with less income may be able to buy only the necessities. Organizations are also concerned with economics and want to buy what they need for reasonable prices in order to earn a profit. Education and demographics are factors that influence consumer buying behavior. Authority is a factor that influences organizational buying behavior.

prompt: A question that is structured so that it requires a broad response rather than a yes/no answer is known as a(n) __________ question.
explanation: Open-ended. Open-ended questions require the respondent to make some kind of statement because they cannot be answered with a yes/no response. A closed-end question is structured so that it requires a short, precise response. An inappropriate question is one that should not be asked, such as questions about age, income, or other personal areas. Open-ended questions are more effective during the early parts of the sales presentation than during the closing.

prompt: What happens if a salesperson is able to sell a substitute service when the customer's request is not available?
choices: The product line can be reduced.
The salesperson has used suggestion selling.
explanation: The business's sales increase. The business's sales increase rather than decrease because a sale is not lost. Suggestion selling is used to sell additional services. Product line is determined from requests of customers and business policy.

prompt: Which of the following methods for handling objections would involve turning the customer's objection into a valid reason for buying:
explanation: Toss-it-back. The toss-it-back method is designed to turn the customer's objection into a valid reason for buying. For example, the salesperson could "toss back" a customer's objection that a car is too large by pointing out how much comfort the car's size provides. The yes, but . . . method acknowledges the objection tactfully and answers it courteously and objectively without directly contradicting the customer. The deny-it method seeks to correct wrong information or a misunderstanding the customer may have. The point-counterpoint method allows the salesperson to agree on a valid point and then answer with an equal or superior point.

prompt: At what point in the sales presentation should a salesperson start using techniques to try to close a sale?
choices: From the initial contact with a customer
At the end of the sales presentation
In the middle of the sales presentation
When a customer states an objection
explanation: From the initial contact with a customer. The close really begins when the salesperson starts the sales presentation. From the first contact with the customer, the salesperson is trying to close. If the salesperson waits until the middle or the end of the sales presentation to use closing techniques, then the salesperson may have missed some valuable opportunities to get the customer to agree to the purchase and close the sale. The salesperson's closing techniques should begin well before a customer starts objecting to the sale so that they can utilize their selling skills to increase the likelihood of a purchase throughout the sales presentation.
